Checks run: grammar labels and positional claims against the line; cross-references; Greek to `l` word by word; `l` against `i`; remembered English; quotation marks and `mark`; line-division of `l` against `t` (all equal); `i` free of `\n`; `p` flags (308, 349, 361, 363, 382, 386, all present); `ln` of every unit; unit ends; every phrase of three or more words checked against all of odyssey-001..094 and the conventions table.

Eurycleia's third speech starts at 403, in the next part, and unit 402 correctly ends on the introduction with no quotation mark.

## Scansion (flagged line 400)

παῖ-δα νέ-ον γε-γα-ῶ-τα κι-χή-σα-το θυ-γα-τέ-ρος ἧς: five dactyls fit only if θυ- (foot 5) is lengthened, and the last foot needs -ρος long, which it is only through the digamma of ἧς (ϝῆς). So the line is irregular as transmitted, at precisely the two places the note already names (fifth foot, sixth foot). Note kept as it stands; no other line in the packet was flagged.

## Findings considered and refused

- **310–311, closing ” missing** although the published unit (odyssey-076, 083 at 537, 164) ends with ”. There the speech ended; here Penelope's speech runs on to 334, so a ” would close it early. Draft left correct. If the validator compares quotation marks it will need an exception for this unit.
- **312 i "and so it will"** for περ: a little padded, but it carries περ and does not change the force. Left.
- **313–316 γε of εἴ ποτ’ ἔην γε not rendered.** The shipped identical clause (odyssey-074 at 267) is "if ever he was" in both layers; kept for consistency.
- **344–347 l "the one wise and trusty"** for κεδνὰ ἰδυῖα is odd English but is the shipped house row for Eurycleia (`l` that phrase, `i` "trusty and wise"). Kept; the note still glosses the two words correctly.
- **325–328 i drops γάρ ("For how …").** Acceptable in prose; `l` has it.
- **340 i "when I passed sleepless nights"** for ὡς τὸ πάρος περ ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον: a temporal gloss, same sense. Left.
- **336–339 ἤχθεθ’** person and number of the form are not stated; the note does not claim them, so nothing false. Left.
- **340 κείω** "exact class of the form is disputed" is a hedge, not an error (short-vowel subjunctive with future sense is the usual view). Left.
- **363 περί called an adverb with the genitive of comparison.** A recognised analysis; not wrong.
- **379–381 i "I tell you I have never yet seen anyone look as much like …".** "Seen" and "I tell you" are interpretive but do not change the claim of φημι … ἰδέσθαι. Left.
- **392–393 l "washed" against i "began to wash"** for the imperfect νίζε: consistent with the note and with the shipped treatment of 387. Left.
- **336 l "were hateful" against i "became hateful":** a free choice for ἤχθεθ’. Left.
- **363 mark "Eurycleia speaks":** her speech answers nothing said to her, so "speaks" is right.
- **356 ἥ σε πόδας νίψει** (ἥ the pronoun 'she', not the relative of 354): true but not needed; the `l` and `i` read it correctly. Not added.
- **Remembered English:** no `i` phrase looked like a ready-made modern rendering; the plain choices ("keep warm", "turn his thoughts to his meal", "the whole matter … out in the open") come from the house table or the case relations.
- **Segmentation:** units ending at a comma (336–339, 370–371, 392–394) all pass the four-line rule; the rest end at · . ; or ;.

## Findings considered and refused (pass 2)

- **λέβης "cauldron".** Published odyssey-002 (unit at 136) and odyssey-013 (unit at 440) say "basin"; the table row 15.84 says "cauldron". The units keep "cauldron" as the owner decided; the conflict between the table and two published parts is flagged at the foot of `new-renderings.md`.
- **ἀτιτάλλω "fostered"** (353): published parts render the verb "rear" or "raise", but "fostered" avoids repeating "reared" for τρέφω in the same clause and no table row is contradicted. Left; flagged in `new-renderings.md`.
- **395 i "other men"** for ἀνθρώπους: "other" is implied by the comparison and idiomatic; left.
- **392 i "had once struck him"** for the aorist ἤλασε in a relative clause: acceptable narrative pluperfect sense; left.
- **344 l "the one wise and trusty"** for κεδνὰ ἰδυῖα: confirmed as the table row (line 166: `l` "the one wise and trusty", `i` "trusty and wise"); pass 1's refusal stands.
- **313 γε, 325 γάρ, 340 περ, 336 ἤχθεθ’, 379–381, 392–393** and the other pass-1 refusals were re-read against the Greek and stand.
- **Pass-1 note edits** (τεύξῃ future middle, ἔην, κάτθετε, θαλπιόων, τάων, σοῖο, κατέσχετο, Hermes/θεός apposition, 335 and 336 notes) re-checked against the lines: all true.
- **Scansion of 400** re-done by hand (17 syllables: five dactyls and the closing spondee; θυ- lengthened to fill the fifth-foot longum, -ρος long only by the digamma of ϝῆς): the note's two places are exactly right.
- **Glossary parses** not listed above were each checked against the line (case, number, gender, tense, voice, mood) and are correct; the 21 other `__broaden__` additions are all true of their lines and need no change. The 141 shipped entries that use ‘ rather than ’ are not this part's concern.
